title: Most beloved deed
lines: Ibn Mas‘ud asked the Prophet ﷺ:
“Which deed is most beloved to Allah?”
quote_en: Prayer at its proper time. Then kindness to parents. Then striving in the way of Allah.
arabic: الصلاة على وقتها ثم بر الوالدين ثم الجهاد في سبيل الله
translation_note: Text verified on Shamela. Ibn Mas‘ud is the narrator (question about 'most beloved').
yt_title: Ibn Mas‘ud Asked About the 3 Deeds Allah Loves Most

shamela.book: صحيح البخاري - ت البغا (no. 504 in this ed.)

arabic_key: الصلاة على وقتها ثم بر الوالدين ثم الجهاد في سبيل الله

title: Who deserves my kindness
lines: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ:
“Who has the most right to my good company?”
quote_en: Your mother. Then your mother. Then your mother. Then your father.
arabic: أمك ثم أمك ثم أمك ثم أبوك
translation_note: Opening verified on Shamela (Abu Hurayrah); full sequence per Bukhari — read page once before posting. Narrator: Abu Hurayrah.
yt_title: 3 Times Mother. Who Did the Prophet ﷺ Name 4th?

shamela.book: صحيح البخاري - ت البغا (no. 5626 in this ed.)

arabic_key: أمك ثم أمك ثم أمك ثم أبوك

title: One thing to hold on to
lines: “Tell me one thing about Islam, so I need ask no one else.”
quote_en: Say: I believe in Allah — then be steadfast.
translation_note: Verified verbatim. Wording is 'fa-staqim' (so be steadfast) in Muslim.

title: Best part of Islam
lines: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ:
quote_en: That you feed people, and greet those you know and those you do not know.
arabic: تطعم الطعام وتقرأ السلام على من عرفت ومن لم تعرف
translation_note: Verified verbatim. Narrated by ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr about a man who asked.
yt_title: Feed People, Greet Everyone: The Prophet's ﷺ Answer
arabic_key: تطعم الطعام وتقرأ السلام على من عرفت ومن لم تعرف
